I have been farming this land in Quzhou for 40 years, and I know what works here. My family has six people, but some of the younger ones work off-farm, so I cannot rely on too much family labor during peak times. That is why I stick to the wheat-maize double cropping on most of my 10.9 mu — it is reliable, and the inputs are easier to manage. I also keep 2 mu of cotton for cash income, because cotton prices have been decent and I have the well water to support it.

For the **winter wheat** on 8.9 mu, I will sow an improved variety in mid-October, just like every year. I learned from the extension agent that 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I have seen that if I push it a bit higher the wheat fills better and I sleep easier. So I will apply about 25 kg of nitrogen per mu — some as urea and some in compound fertilizer — plus about 12 kg of phosphorus and 3 kg of potassium from the compound bag. I will till with rotary tillage before sowing to break up the stubble, and irrigate four times: once before winter freeze, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain filling. I expect about 500 kg per mu if the weather cooperates. For pesticides, I spray three times — herbicide once and insecticide twice — because the aphids always come back.

For **summer maize** on the same 8.9 mu, I plant right after wheat harvest in mid-June with no time to waste. I use a hybrid variety because the yield is much better than the old types. I will put down about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu, plus 2 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. Maize does not need as much water as wheat if the summer rains come, but I will irrigate twice to be safe — once at the big喇叭口 stage and once at flowering. I spray for pests and weeds twice. With good luck, I can get 550 kg per mu.

For **cotton** on 2 mu, I plant in late April after rotary tillage. I use an improved cotton variety. Cotton is thirsty and needs fertilizer, so I give it about 15 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate three times during the growing season, especially when the bolls are forming. Cotton attracts more insects, so I spray five or six times — I would rather spend a bit more on pesticide than lose the bolls to bollworms. I expect around 250 kg of seed cotton per mu.

I do not change much from year to year because change is risky. I have the well, so water is not my biggest worry; my biggest worry is labor during harvest and whether input prices go up. I use round numbers and buy what I can afford, but I always make sure the wheat gets enough fertilizer — a bad wheat harvest is a disaster for my family.
